page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n4 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel x86_64 cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The underlying Intel processor includes a cache hierarchy consisting of a 48 KB L1 data cache, a 2 MB L2 cache, and a 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512f, AVX512_VNNI, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) for matrix math acceleration. Cryptographic operations are assisted by AES, VAES, and SHA_NI hardware flags.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1807.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1561.99. However, multi-core and memory subsystem benchmarks fall into the lower 25th percentile, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4100.0 and a Passmark memory score of 1557.54. Memory bandwidth is limited, measuring 32.36 GB/sec for large-block reads and 21.01 GB/sec for large-block writes.

Given its balanced resource ratio and moderate single-threaded execution speeds, this server is suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 6.53 GB/sec. It is also capable of handling light text processing and basic single-threaded compression tasks. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded software compilation, or complex ray tracing due to its lower multi-core and memory bandwidth performance.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel processor with 2 physical cores and hyper-threading, it includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs. Performance benchmarks show average single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1807.0, but weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth results, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 4100.0 and 32.36 GB/sec uncached read speeds. It is suited for moderate, balanced workloads like static web serving, light text processing, and basic single-threaded applications, while being less optimal for heavy multi-threaded computing or memory-bound database operations.
